findings.evidence: The proof body at lines 196-197 uses only `trans_assoc`, `mk_trans` and `eq`; `Path.Homotopic.Quotient.trans_assoc` exists in Mathlib (mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroupoid/Basic.lean:220), so the `mk`-free statement is provable with the same one-line proof. Neighbouring API in this file (`subpath_trans`, `eq_of_trans_symm`, lines 122, 180) is stated at quotient level.
findings.fix: State the general form and derive this one: `theorem trans_trans_suffix_eq {A : Quotient p q} {B : Quotient q r} {C : Quotient p s} {D : Quotient s r} (h : trans A B = trans C D) (suffix : Quotient r w) : trans A (trans B suffix) = trans C (trans D suffix) := by rw [← trans_assoc, ← trans_assoc, h]`. Keep the `_of_homotopic` variant only if wanted, as `trans_trans_suffix_eq (by rw [← mk_trans, ← mk_trans, eq]; exact h) suffix`.
findings.issue: `mk_trans_trans_suffix_eq_of_homotopic` restricts the hypothesis to a path-level `Homotopic` between `a.trans b` and `c.trans d` and both sides to `mk` of literal paths, but the fact proved is purely quotient-level: from `trans A B = trans C D` one gets `trans A (trans B suffix) = trans C (trans D suffix)` by `trans_assoc` alone. A consumer whose classes are quotient variables (or come from quotient-level lemmas such as the `@[simp] subpath_trans` at line 122 of this same file) cannot apply it without first exhibiting representative paths.

summary: Only one new public declaration, but it is stated in a needlessly specialized `mk`/`Homotopic` form when the underlying fact is a pure quotient-level consequence of `trans_assoc`, so consumers holding a quotient equality cannot use it. Everything else is correctly private and the public signature is unchanged.
